A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUnsET research. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data analyses, citation and summary evaluations, positional-bias measurements, and training-size experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds fixed-granularity comparisons, human assessment of SUnsET, topic-diversity measurements, and citation-summary correlations.

M1.justification: The six-stage generation pipeline, standard and shuffled LoRA training, and chunk-summarize-combine inference are retained. Appendix A's generation, training, and inference prompts match. Renaming Standard to SUnsET does not introduce a method component; omitted procedural details are assessed under D1.

E1.justification: Both versions use SUnsET and the same four downstream datasets: SQuALITY, LexAbSumm, SummHay, and ScholarQABench. Their single-document, multi-document, literary, legal, scientific, and synthetic coverage remains unchanged. The added validation analyses reuse these data.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated Fixed Gran. comparator for each of the five open LLMs across the four datasets, substantially expanding the central comparisons beyond unstructured base models and GPT-4o-mini. The earlier synthetic-generation baselines are retained under the names Non-Pipelined and Title + Doc.

E3.justification: The main relevance and consistency evaluator changes from GPT-4o-mini to DeepSeek-V3. v2 also introduces a two-annotator, 100-example assessment using three-point ratings and an LDA-based topic-diversity evaluation. Section 4.1 changes the stated precision averaging unit from citing sentences to citations. These changes materially affect evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds human validation of summary responsiveness, organization, and evidential support; topic-diversity comparisons with human-written corpora; and correlations between citation and summary quality. The training-size ablations move from v1 Figures 6–7 to v2 Figures 23–24. The existing 710-summary cross-evaluator correlation check is retained.

E5.justification: v2 extends significance annotations to evidence quality and citation F1, explicitly using non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals against both baselines. v1 specifies bootstrapped intervals for summary comparisons, whereas v2 omits the interval-construction method. v2 also reports human annotator agreement of 93.67%; neither version specifies repeated training runs or random seeds.

E6.justification: Citation F1 and summary-quality scores are extensively replaced, and fixed-granularity, separate precision/recall, and validation results are added. For example, Llama 3.1 8B with standard training has SQuALITY relevance F1 of 35.21 in v1 Table 3 and 27.69 in v2 Table 6; the changed evaluator and metric specification prevent interpreting this as a same-setting decline. Evidence-copy results remain identical in v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated precision definition from averaging over citances, meaning citing sentences, to averaging over citations. These differ when a sentence contains multiple citations. This is a limited mathematical specification change; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v2 adds a central claim that unstructured evidence, especially after SUnsET training, outperforms fixed-granularity evidence, extending v1's claims about improvements over untuned models. The introduction also adds claims of high synthetic-data quality and diversity comparable to human-written data. The original task, dataset, and positional-bias contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of citation quality versus coverage and why selecting evidence before summarization may improve summaries. It revises the positional-bias interpretation: standard training can reduce bias, and shuffled training has an explicit Mixtral exception. It also explains training-size plateaus through distribution coverage and adds a limitation concerning differences between synthetic and human-written text.

D1.justification: v2 documents topic-model parameters, DeepSeek-V3 sampling settings, and approximately $200 in generation costs. It omits v1's 200-document validation/early-stopping holdout and five-attempt formatting retry rule, without establishing that those procedures changed. Training hyperparameters, hardware, model identifiers, prompts, and the public MIT-licensed code/data release are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on summary-source alignment, citation planning, precise evidence, and topic diversity, including Ernst, Fierro, Wan, Xiao, and Terragni. Several general motivation and evaluation references disappear. The MDCure publication update and Sentence-BERT bibliographic correction concern already-cited works, rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, an explicit contribution list is added, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around fixed-granularity comparisons and aggregate results. Dataset-specific discussion and training-size analysis are reorganized into appendices. This is extensive narrative restructuring despite the retained method and prompts.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, adds the fixed-versus-unstructured example and topic-diversity table, and introduces aggregate bar charts with expanded appendix tables. Evidence-position histograms are merged and redrawn as density curves, omitting the former 1B panel. Training-size plots are relocated unchanged, and Table 1 is compacted by removing title columns.

improvement.justification: The fixed-granularity comparisons and independent human assessment of SUnsET address important gaps in v1's support for its central formulation and synthetic training data. Topic-diversity analysis and separate citation precision/recall results further strengthen that support. Omitted validation/retry details and less explicit confidence-interval methodology weaken reproducibility, but the gains in evaluating the central claims are substantial overall.
